sources.limits: It is a loop macro rather than a first-class sequence by itself, and adopting its grammar or lowering does not automatically settle Python name-binding or mutation semantics. sources.title: SRFI-1 iota and its public reference implementation
sources.version_or_date: Live SRFI-1 text revised through 2026-10-03; historical final status 1999-10-09
sources.sections_read: Status; constructors/iota; reference implementation availability and portability notes.
sources.confirmed: iota builds count elements beginning at start and separated by step, defaulting to zero and one; the canonical standard declares final status on 1999-10-09 and supplies public reference code. The exact live text has later errata, so it is not treated as a frozen 1999 document.
sources.limits: It takes a count rather than an end boundary and eagerly constructs a list, so converting end-based uses may add the arithmetic the problem seeks to remove; it remains an ordinary named procedure, and the current evidence is not a frozen pre-cutoff version. sources.title: Haskell 1.3 arithmetic-sequence notation and Prelude-bound translation
sources.version_or_date: Haskell 1.3 report; official edition index dates version 1.3 to May 1996
sources.sections_read: Expression translation binding rules and section 3.10 Arithmetic Sequences.
sources.confirmed: Haskell 1.3 represents arithmetic sequences with a start, optional second element that determines the increment, and optional terminal bound. Translation uses Prelude Enum methods rather than arbitrary locally rebound names, while type-class instances still determine enumeration behavior.
sources.limits: The increment is inferred from the first two values, the terminal boundary is inclusive, and zero increment can produce an infinite sequence; Enum overloading still prevents treating every instance as primitive integer arithmetic. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C09.json.

sources.title: Python 2.0 range and xrange
sources.version_or_date: Python 2.0 Library Reference, 2000-10-16; confirmed by opened parent title page
sources.sections_read: range and xrange entries; release-string search.
sources.confirmed: range accepts start/stop/step, uses an exclusive terminal bound, and rejects a zero step; xrange supplies the corresponding numbers without storing them all simultaneously. The retrieved page alone gives no release date.
sources.limits: The terminal boundary is exclusive and step zero is rejected; retaining ordinary calls retains nested-call readability costs and the rebinding constraint, so optimization needs binding proof or a guard, and fixed index bounds do not make length-changing mutations safe. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C09.json.

sources.title: FORTRAN 77 DO loop control
sources.version_or_date: Sun/Oracle FORTRAN 77 Language Reference; publication date not yet established
sources.sections_read: DO syntax, evaluation of bounds/increment, iteration count, terminal processing, restrictions, overflow note.
sources.confirmed: FORTRAN DO expresses start, terminal bound, and increment directly, evaluates those parameters when entering the loop, and establishes an iteration count. It prohibits changing the DO variable in the body and warns about overflow.
sources.limits: This is a loop construct rather than a sequence value, uses an inclusive terminal bound, restricts changes to the loop variable, and has overflow caveats; the retrieved manual's publication date was not established. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C09.json.

sources.title: Scheme R5RS do iteration and hygienic expansion
sources.version_or_date: R5RS report, 1998 edition as identified by archive bibliography
sources.sections_read: Sections 4.2.4 Iteration and 4.3 Macros; primitive/derived distinction.
sources.confirmed: Scheme do combines initialization, a termination test, and per-iteration update expressions, with a vector-mutation example. The report specifies hygienic macro expansion with definition-site binding for inserted references, while explicitly allowing local bindings to shadow syntactic keywords.
sources.limits: The form is more verbose than a range expression; tests and update expressions execute each iteration, local bindings can shadow syntactic keywords, and user-supplied operators still require their normal binding semantics. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C09.json.
